Question: Who holds zoning authority
Pennsylvania: Municipalities (about 2,500 boroughs, townships and cities); county ordinances apply where a township has none
Ohio: Cities (home rule), townships and counties; township zoning is optional, and many rural townships have none

Question: Statewide deadlines for local decisions
Pennsylvania: Conditional use: hearing within 60 days, decision within 45 days after last hearing; county review 30 days; land development plan within 90 days
Virginia: Planning commission: 100 days; county governing body: 12 months; site plans: 40 days
Ohio: Township rezoning: hearing 20–40 days after filing; recommendation within 30 days; trustee hearing within 30 days; decision within 20 days
Georgia: Hearing notice 15–45 days ahead; regional review up to 30 days; no decision deadline found

Question: If the local deadline is missed
Virginia: Planning commission is deemed to recommend approval; no deemed approval for the governing body

Question: Voter referendum on a rezoning
Ohio: Yes: township voters can petition within 30 days of adoption; megaproject rezonings exempt since Sept. 2026, and large data centers are not excluded from that definition
Maryland: No: courts ruled Frederick County's data center ordinance not subject to referendum (June 2026, as reported)

Question: Regional or county review layer
Pennsylvania: County planning agency reviews land development plans (advisory; 30 days)
Ohio: County or regional planning commission recommends (advisory)
Maryland: None statewide; Montgomery and Prince George's use a bi-county planning commission
Georgia: Regional commission reviews large projects within 30 days and takes comment; locality cannot give final approval until it ends

Question: State-required site or impact disclosure
Pennsylvania: None statewide; GRID Requirements notice under the executive order
Virginia: Site assessment for 100 MW or more, including sound at homes and schools within 500 feet
Maryland: Registry with the PSC, energy and water use, from January 2027
Georgia: Water and electricity estimates in regional review

Question: Does state environmental review wait on local approval?
Can the state override local review?
Ohio: Yes: a Power Siting Board certificate for on-site power plants replaces local review (Hilliard, 72.9 MW, 2025)
Maryland: No; qualifying backup generators skip PSC approval but not local zoning

Question: Backup generators
Pennsylvania: Executive order directs DEP to examine emission rules
Virginia: Tier 4 generators required for new data centers (2026, as reported)
Maryland: MDE permit to construct; no PSC approval if backup-only and no grid export
Georgia: EPD air permits by size; synthetic minor common for large fleets

Question: Large-load tariff
Pennsylvania: PUC tentative order; final vote targeted Jan. 28, 2027
Virginia: Dominion GS-5, 25 MW and up; effective Jan. 1, 2027
Ohio: AEP Ohio, 25 MW and up; in effect since July 23, 2025
Maryland: 25 MW and 60% load factor (May 2026 law); tariffs filed Sept. 1, PSC review under way
Georgia: Georgia Power, over 100 MW; in effect since Jan. 2025 (contracts up to 15 years)

Question: Legislature in 2026
Pennsylvania: No siting law enacted. HB 2674, barring data centers from public utility status, which the sponsor says could otherwise let developers override local zoning, passed the House 202–1 on Oct. 19 and is in the Senate.
Virginia: Site assessment law (SB 94/HB 153); Tier 4 generators for new data centers
Ohio: Bills pending (study commission, siting limits, NDA ban); 2025 law eased on-site power
